svg.title: 3. Hybrid DNS with Route 53 Resolver
svg.text: Hybrid DNS: Route 53 Resolver endpoints in one shared VPC, rules and zones handed out with a Route 53 Profile
rule, the PHZ and DNS Firewall rules.
DNS Firewall arrive with zero clicks.
endpoint's private IPs, so backups go over DX
orders-api asks the VPC Resolver for erp.corp.example.
The forwarding rule from the Profile matches, so
Resolver sends the query out of the outbound
endpoint, over DX, to both AD DNS servers.
Answers are cached for the record's TTL.
AD DNS has a conditional forwarder for
aws.corp.example pointing at the 3 inbound IPs.
Resolver answers from the private hosted zone
and checks DNS Firewall. Never forward "." or
corp.example back the other way: that is a loop.
For each interface endpoint on-prem should use,
AD DNS forwards that service name (for example
Traffic then rides DX to private IPs instead of
the internet, and stays off the NAT bill.
Sizing: one IP per AZ to start, watch the endpoint's query metrics, add IPs before peak. Restrictive security groups turn on connection tracking, which lowers per-IP capacity a lot.
